summary.headline: IGI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23% YoY to INR 3,708 million and EBITDA 29% to INR 2,238 million, with 60.4% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated certification revenue grew 23% YoY to INR 3,598 million on 17% volume growth, with LGD, LGD Jewellery and the newly consolidated AGL gemstones segment all contributing. Group EBITDA rose 29% to INR 2,238 million and margin expanded 270 bps to 60.4%, while PAT grew 31% to INR 1,657 million. India standalone growth was slower on EBITDA (15%) because of commission payouts to overseas subsidiaries, front-loaded IPL sponsorship and headcount additions. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA growth, with AGL adding a couple of percentage points on top.

segments.name: LGD loose stones (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Grew 25% YoY; management cites growing grower capacity and consumer demand as drivers, with volume the main growth impetus.

segments.name: LGD Jewellery (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Grew 44% YoY; India standalone LGD Jewellery grew 38%.

segments.name: Gemstones and other certification
segments.commentary: Grew over 200% YoY, reflecting the AGL consolidation; India standalone gemstones grew 135%. AGL added about 3% to revenue growth, with the base business growing 20%.

segments.name: Natural diamond loose stones
segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY in the quarter, a slowdown from the double-digit growth of recent quarters; management says it is a strategic priority focused on market share gains.

segments.name: Natural diamond jewellery
segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY after a decline in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: India standalone LGD
segments.commentary: LGD certification revenue grew 30% YoY on standalone basis.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained at 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth; management said it is early days after one quarter.
AGL is expected to add a couple of percentage points to revenue growth on top of the 15% base-business guidance.
Group EBITDA margin expected to improve by at least 100 bps by end of FY27, supported by operating leverage.
India standalone EBITDA margin expected to stabilise in the 70% range as discretionary brand and marketing spends moderate.
Management expects group EBITDA growth to exceed revenue growth over the next three quarters.
capex_capacity: Growers reportedly plan to double their business over the next three years, per management; capacity additions are driving LGD volume growth.
Incremental capex is linked to volume and scale-up; finance costs rose due to higher rent on additional office space. The company remains debt-free.
Certification capacity is being expanded in technical and process staff to shorten turnaround time; management said 2-3 days is an acceptable TAT.
AGL plans to set up collection and mobile laboratory operations, starting in Jaipur, with later extension to other geographies.
Operations commenced in Italy through the Belgium subsidiary; US investments are beginning to show traction.
demand_pricing: Wholesale LGD pricing has been stable at roughly INR 80-120 per carat over the last two years; the last price correction was in April-May 2024, when LGD realisation fell about 25%.
Blended realisation growth of 5% is attributed about 2-3 points to AGL and 2 points to base-business mix, with higher carat size in LGD reports cited as a factor.
Consolidated EBITDA margin was 58% in Q1 and about 61% for FY26 per management, while the India margin was described as 70-74% over the last couple of years.
Management said the top 12-14 LGD growers account for about 80% of lab-grown stones made in India; the top 8-10 contribute about 40-50% of revenue.
Management said the company holds the highest natural diamond market share in India; global ND share gains are the focus.
Management reported a turnaround-time target of two to three days and said AI/ML is being used to cut processing time.

qa_highlights.question: How will LGD pricing per report evolve as grower capacity expands, and will volume growth force price concessions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rising consumer demand for affordable LGD keeps growers expanding, and that certification by IGI is what makes an LGD stone a diamond; no pricing pressure was specifically quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% revenue guidance inclusive of AGL?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the 15% applies to the base business, with AGL adding a couple of percentage points on top.

qa_highlights.question: How much was the IPL marketing spend in the quarter and what was the employee addition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR 5 crore was spent on sponsorship and marketing in the quarter, with additional leadership investments; management said headcount was added for technical and process staff, but the number was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the realisation improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed about 2-3 points of the 5% ASP growth to AGL and about 2% to base-business mix; underlying pricing is described as stable, and higher carat per report was cited.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the international EBITDA margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to leads from overseas retailers, with commission payouts from India to these geographies recorded in other expenses; operating leverage was said to flow through similarly to India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the commission payout to subsidiaries material, and what is the standalone EBITDA ex-commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to isolate it, saying the India and overseas businesses are interdependent and the consolidated margin should be the focus; it confirmed incremental consolidated EBITDA is the relevant measure.

qa_highlights.question: How many LGD growers exist and what is the capacity growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give capacity figures; growers are reported to be talking about doubling their business over three years, with US-led demand and increasing India demand.

risks_watch: Natural diamond loose stone growth slowed to 6% from double-digit prior quarters; management has not quantified share gain targets.
Concentration risk: the top 8-10 LGD growers account for about 40-50% of revenue, per management.
Margin dilution from commission payouts to overseas geographies and continued brand and headcount investment; the India margin is guided to the 70% range.
Realisation is exposed to mix swings: management said jewellery mix increases have historically caused dips in ASP, and the Diwali quarters are a risk.
Q1 was flagged by management as early in the year, so FY27 guidance was kept unchanged despite a strong start.
Turnaround time was described as lengthening by one analyst on the ground; management said TAT depends on volumes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and growth, and tight on guidance; management kept the 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA targets unchanged after a strong Q1. It was defensive when pushed on standalone margins, commission payouts and LGD pricing, and declined to give detailed carat or certification splits, citing competitive reasons.
key_quotes: We have begun FY27 on a strong note, delivering Q1 revenue growth at 23% and an EBITDA growth of 29% year-on-year.
As the discretionary spends moderate, we expect the EBITDA margins to stabilize in the 70% range.
Underlying pricing has remained, you know, consistent or constant since the last time we did a correction, which was April-May of 2024 on natural pricing on LGD.
